analysis.title: US Economic Notes: What you need to know for the week ahead
key_insights: The week's holiday-shortened calendar centers on NY Fed President Williams' keynote on Monday and Wednesday's October personal income and consumption report, which carries the core PCE deflator, the Fed's preferred inflation measure.
Williams is scheduled to have the last word before the Fed's communications blackout ahead of the December 9 FOMC meeting.

Fed communication over the past two weeks has been uniformly hawkish. Williams said last Tuesday that the Fed still has work to do to bring inflation back to 2% but did not see a need for 'dramatic action', which downplays an outsized hike in December.
DB does not expect the roughly 5% S&P 500 decline since Williams last spoke to change his message on the need for further tightening.

The October FOMC minutes show the Fed discussing financial stability risks from rapid AI-related debt growth, naming elevated asset valuations and hedge fund leverage as the most salient vulnerabilities. Williams could cite this discussion.

Governor Cook said last Friday that financial conditions are too accommodative with inflation above target and that policy is not curtailing the AI buildout. DB reads the drop in risk assets as not yet having fazed the Fed.
DB raised its Q4 real GDP growth forecast by 60bps to 2.5% after strong October retail sales.

DB expects today's S&P Global PMIs and Tuesday's consumer confidence to edge higher on a healthy labor market and sturdy AI-related business demand. Wednesday's durable goods orders should confirm strong AI-related capex demand.
DB forecasts October core PCE at +0.29% m/m against +0.32% consensus. With no revisions to past data this equals 3.23% y/y, the highest since November 2023.
DB projects 25bp Fed hikes at each of the next three meetings, taking the fed funds rate to 4.625% by end of Q1 2027.

Tighter conditions from AI-related reassessment of valuations, wider credit spreads and falling equities are not yet enough to replace rate hikes. A larger extension in magnitude and duration could give the Fed pause.

risk_factors: Further declines in equities and wider credit spreads tied to AI-related valuation concerns could give the Fed pause on tightening.
AI-related debt growth, elevated asset valuations and hedge fund leverage are cited by the October FOMC minutes as the most salient financial stability vulnerabilities.
An outsized rate hike in December is downplayed by Williams but remains a risk if inflation data runs hot.

tension_points.theme: AI valuation selloff vs Fed tightening
tension_points.bull_case: Falling equities and wider credit spreads tighten financial conditions, which could substitute for rate hikes and give the Fed pause.
tension_points.bear_case: The tightening is not yet sufficient to replace the need for hikes. Fed officials Williams and Cook remain hawkish and Cook says policy is not curtailing the AI buildout.
tension_points.what_invalidates: An extension of the equity and credit moves in magnitude and duration would give the Fed pause.

theme_stances.key_argument: The Fed is likely to keep tightening because the current tightening in financial conditions is not yet enough to replace rate hikes.
theme_stances.evidence: this tightening is not yet sufficient to replace the need for rate hikes
